Back exercise

Lat Pulldown

The lat pulldown is a machine version of the pull-up that lets you choose the load. It is the go-to exercise for building the lats when you cannot yet do pull-ups or want extra back volume.

By Khushi Gupta · Reviewed October 2026

Primary
Back
Also works
Lats, Biceps, Rear delts, Lower traps
Equipment
Cable pulldown machine
Level
Beginner

How to do it

  1. Adjust the thigh pad so your legs are locked in snugly with feet flat on the floor.
  2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with palms facing away.
  3. Sit down with arms fully extended overhead and lean back slightly, about 10 to 20 degrees.
  4. Pull your shoulder blades down first, then drive your elbows down toward your sides.
  5. Bring the bar to your upper chest, just below your collarbone.
  6. Squeeze your back briefly, then let the bar rise under control until your arms are straight and you feel a stretch in your lats.

Coaching cues

  • Elbows down to your pockets
  • Chest up to meet the bar
  • Control the way up
  • Slight lean, no swinging
Advertisements

Common mistakes and fixes

Leaning back and yanking the weight

Keep a fixed, slight lean and use a weight you can pull without rocking your torso.

Pulling the bar behind the neck

Pull to the front of your chest. Behind-the-neck pulldowns stress the shoulder joint for no added benefit.

Stopping short at the top

Let your arms straighten fully so the lats get a full stretch.

Pulling with the biceps

Think of your hands as hooks and drive with the elbows.

Sets and reps

GoalPrescription
Strength4 sets of 6-8 reps, 2 minutes rest
Hypertrophy3-4 sets of 8-15 reps, 90 seconds rest
Beginner3 sets of 10-12 reps with a controlled tempo

Pick a starting weight with the one rep max calculator, and load the bar with the plate calculator.

Variations

  • Close neutral grip pulldown A V-handle; usually allows heavier loads with comfortable shoulders.
  • Underhand pulldown More biceps and lower lat involvement.
  • Single-arm cable pulldown Fixes imbalances and increases range.
  • Straight-arm pulldown Isolates the lats without elbow bending.

Muscles worked

The latissimus dorsi pulls the upper arm down and back, assisted by the teres major, lower traps and rhomboids. The biceps and forearms bend the elbow.

Benefits

Because you set the load, pulldowns let beginners train the same pattern as a pull-up long before they can lift their bodyweight. They also make it easy to add back volume late in a session when you are tired.

Build toward pulling roughly your bodyweight for 8 reps and a strict pull-up is usually close.

Safety and who should modify it

The pulldown is very joint friendly. If your shoulders feel pinched, use a neutral grip and avoid pulling the bar lower than your upper chest.

Frequently asked questions

Is the lat pulldown as good as pull-ups?

For muscle growth it is very similar. Pull-ups add more core work and are a better test of strength relative to bodyweight.

Wide grip or close grip?

A grip slightly wider than shoulders suits most people. Very wide grips shorten the range and do not build a wider back.

Should I lean back?

Slightly, about 10 to 20 degrees, so the bar clears your face. Leaning far back turns it into a row.
